entity.description: ABB Group is a Swedish-Swiss technology company, that operates in the fields of electrification and automation. The company was formed in 1988 from the merger of two electrical engineering companies, [ASEA](en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASEA) of Sweden and [Brown, Boveri & Cie](en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown,_Boveri_&amp)(BBC) of Switzerland. Incorporated in Switzerland as ABB Ltd, and headquartered in [Zurich](en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zurich), it is [dual-listed](en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dual-listed_compan) on the [Nasdaq Nordic](en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasdaq_Nordic) exchange in [Stockholm](en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm), Sweden, and the [SIX Swiss Exchange](en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIX_Swiss_Exchange) in Zurich., in addition to [OTC Markets Group's](en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OTC_Markets_Group) pink sheets in the United States. For 30 years, it has been a part of the [Fortune Global 500](en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune_Global_500). Employees of ABB and its predecessor companies developed several technologies for generating, transmitting, and distributing electricity, as well as for enabling industrial automation. One is the miniature circuit breaker, invented by Hugo Stotz, which protects against fires and is found in almost every home. Predecessor ASEA was the first company to introduce a microprocessor into an industrial robot and it helped to develop the electric propulsion system "Azipod", which improved manoeuvrability by locating the propulsion system outside the hull. ABB is made up of around 20 divisions structured into four business areas: Electrification, Motion, Process Automation and Robotics & Discrete Automation. Previously, it had a large power grids business, which was sold to Hitachi in 2020, as well as a turbocharging business, that was spun off in 2022. Over the years, ABB made different acquisitions, with major ones in the 21st century including [Baldor Electric](en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABB_Motors_and_Mec), [Thomas & Betts](en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_&_Betts), and the GE Industrial Solutions division of [General Electric](en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Electric). The company's activities have been the subject of controversy on multiple occasions. US-based Combustion Engineering, acquired by ABB in 1990, exposed the company to [asbestos](en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asbestos)-related litigation, which led to ABB’s first-ever loss in 2001. A final claims settlement was reached in 2006. ABB has also been subject to three US [Foreign Corrupt Practices Act](en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Corrupt_Pr) bribery settlements in 2004, 2010, and 2022. Additionally, in 2001, an ABB entity pleaded guilty to [bid rigging](en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bid_rigging). During the 2010s, ABB largely focused its growth strategy on the robotics and industrial automation sectors.
